page.layout: One text column, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top, with page number "79". Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: tur, ut ita ex eo congressu, fu-turos eventus certò prædicerent. Ejus gentis cum quâ bellum est, captivum quoquo modo interce-ptū cum electo popularium suorum, patriis quemque armis committunt. Victoria hujus vel illius pro præjudi-cio accipitur. Id est, secundum Rævardum,pro præjudicato. Fuit & olim hoc genus certaminis Græcis familiare, imprimis quando res arduas aggredi volebant. Quod etiam suo com-probavit exemplo Magnus ille Alexander, qui dimicaturus cum Persarum Rege Dario, duos produxit milites, quorum alter suam personam sustineret, alter Darii; quâ per-sonâ devictâ[?], quæ pro partibus Plutarchus in vitâ Alexandri. stabat Darii, actutum decrevit bellum, ratus se quoque Darii fore victorem.
Si tamen res ipsa penitius examinanda veniat, dicendum videtur, hoc genus certaminis

page.notes: Marginal notes right: "Tacitus de Moribus Germanorum, Rævard. Præjud. libr. i. c. 1." (printed in several short lines; placed beside the first lines of the paragraph, after "bellum") and "Plutarchus in vitâ Alexandri." (printed in three lines). The note block is placed at its first reference position in the paragraph. Doubtful: "devictâ" in "quâ personâ devictâ" is not clearly legible on the scan. Long s in "suorum", "suo", "est" printed as f/s and transcribed as plain s; "futuros", "Fuit" and "fu-turos" contain a true f and are kept. Catchword "præ-" and signature "D 4" are printed at the foot.
